questions.enonce_markdown:
What role did John the Baptist play in the life and ministry of Jesus Christ?

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** In Luke's Gospel John the Baptist is the forerunner of Jesus: the prophet who prepares Israel for the coming of the Lord. His story is closely woven with that of Jesus from the very beginning.

**1. His birth is linked to that of Jesus.** The angel Gabriel announces John's birth to the priest Zechariah and Jesus' birth to Mary (Luke 1:5-38). John is to be filled with the Holy Spirit from his mother's womb and to go before the Lord "in the spirit and power of Elijah" (1:15-17). Elizabeth's child leaps in her womb when Mary arrives (1:41-44), and Zechariah's song says John will be called "prophet of the Most High" who prepares the way (1:76-79).

**2. He prepares the way by preaching repentance.** John appears in the wilderness proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins, in fulfilment of Isaiah's "voice of one crying in the wilderness" (3:1-6). He demands real change: sharing with the needy, honesty from tax collectors, restraint from soldiers (3:10-14).

**3. He points away from himself.** When the people wonder whether he is the Messiah, John says that one more powerful is coming, who will baptise with the Holy Spirit and fire (3:15-17). He knows that he is not worthy to untie the thong of the sandals.

**4. He is linked to the start of Jesus' ministry.** Jesus is baptised in the period of John's work, the Spirit descends and the voice from heaven declares him Son (3:21-22). Jesus' public ministry follows, and John is soon imprisoned by Herod for rebuking him (3:19-20).

**5. Jesus' witness to John.** John sends disciples from prison to ask whether Jesus is "the one who is to come" (7:18-23). Jesus answers by pointing to his works, then says there is no one greater than John among those born of women, while the least in the kingdom of God is greater (7:24-28). Jesus also says that the law and the prophets were until John, after which the good news of the kingdom is proclaimed (16:16).

**Conclusion.** John is the bridge between the old and new covenants. He is forerunner, preacher of repentance and witness to Jesus, and his role shows that Jesus' ministry fulfils God's promises to Israel.
